searches.reason: Develop paired history interventions that test whether rankings depend on recent repeated interests, isolated old interactions, or already satisfied needs. Compare recency truncation, removal of repeated-interest evidence, and order shuffling; connect ranking changes to the sequence encoder and temporal weighting. Use training-history prefixes without changing benchmark splits, and treat sensitivity as evidence of model dependence rather than proof of user intent.

searches.reason: Find practical ways to turn the supplied qualitative feedback into auditable recommendation-level probes: specific match versus broad relatedness, useful complement versus duplicate, and explicitly supported versus unknown prerequisites. Ground judgments in available titles, descriptions, and histories, retain evidence spans, and report insufficient information separately. Validate the rubric on the twenty observed users without inferring unobserved traits or accessing unavailable metadata.

searches.reason: Replace score-scale-dependent margins and mean cosine with diagnostics whose reliability can be tested. Investigate sampled-candidate versus full-catalog ranking disagreement, popularity-stratified failures, effective embedding rank, and controlled fault injection. Seek probes that reliably detect known model degradations and predict improvements across all four datasets, with uncertainty estimates and bounded GPU cost; reserve pinned validation HR@10 for model selection.
